name: Puente de los Franceses
story: This 19th-century railway bridge over the Manzanares was one of the crossings the Nationalists needed to break into Madrid from the Casa de Campo in November 1936. Republican militias and troops, soon joined by the newly arrived International Brigades, defended it; the fighting here is remembered as part of the Brigades' baptism of fire. It gave its name to a popular Republican song ('Puente de los Franceses, mamita mía, nadie te pasa'). The Nationalists eventually crossed the river further north and entered the University City instead.
see: The original brick-and-granite five-arch bridge, still carrying trains.
plan: View from the Madrid Río riverside path or the Paseo de la Florida; 15 minutes' walk from Príncipe Pío.
